verdict.rationale: The docs describe repo-scoped placement: teams can check in skills for a working folder, Codex scans `.agents/skills` up to the repository root, and repo marketplaces exist alongside local marketplaces. A personal setup path also exists via `$skill-installer` for 'your own local Codex setup'. There is no documented explicit choice of install scope at install time, and plugin (versus skill) install scope is not described. missing for 10: an explicit project-vs-user scope option when installing plugins, documented user-global install paths, hands-on corroboration of committed repo-local plugin installs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can choose install scope — project-local files committed with my repo, or user-global across all projects

citations.quote: teams can check in skills relevant to a working folder. For example, skills only relevant to a microservice or a module.
Codex scans `.agents/skills` in every directory from your current working directory up to the repository root.
To add curated skills beyond the built-ins for your own local Codex setup, use `$skill-installer`.
Local and repo marketplaces are separate authoring, testing, and team-distribution sources, and their availability can vary by surface.
